args.title: Inside the PLC: CPU, power and I O

scenes.narration: Every panel starts with protection. This is the breaker, a three pole, ten amp unit. It protects the cables and the motor from a short circuit. It does not protect the motor from slowly overheating. That job belongs to the overload, which we will meet properly later in this stage.

Here is the controller itself. Inside it, you will find a power supply stage, taking mains power and producing a clean twenty four volt D C control supply. And the C P U, the part that actually runs the program. In a small machine like this, the power supply, C P U and I O are built into one compact unit. On a bigger plant, you would see a modular rack, where each of those is a separate card you can swap out.
caption: Here is the controller. Inside it: a power supply stage, taking mains power and producing a clean
24 volt DC control supply, and the CPU, which runs the program.
On a small machine like this they're built into one compact unit.
On bigger plant, you'd see a modular rack with each as a separate, swappable card.

scenes.narration: And here is the I O. Every input and output has an address. I zero zero is the first input. Q zero zero is the first output. This board is digital, it only sees on or off. Later in this course you will also meet analogue I O, which reads a range, like a current or a level, instead of a simple on or off.

scenes.narration: Let's prove three channels at once. The P L C is running a simple test program, one input straight to one output on each rung. Tap Start, and the run lamp lights, I zero zero driving Q zero one. Tap Stop, and the fault lamp lights, I zero one driving Q zero two. Tap AUX, and the beacon lights, I zero four driving Q zero three. Watch the signal board. The input L E D and the output L E D light together, every time.

scenes.narration: One more idea before we move on. This control runs on twenty four volts D C. Inputs can be wired sourcing or sinking, which just describes which side of the twenty four volts switches. Your site standard decides which one you use. Either way, the P L C only ever sees a clean on or off at the input terminal.
